record.paper_title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
record.original_question: Let C be a class of separable topological groups and let V(C) be the variety generated by C, meaning the intersection of all nonempty classes of topological groups containing C that are closed under taking subgroups, quotient groups, arbitrary cartesian products, and isomorphic images. If the groups in C are not assumed to be abelian, must every metrizable group in V(C) be separable?

evidence.quote: Recall that a non-empty class of topological groups is said to be a variety if it is closed under the operations of taking subgroups, quotient groups, (arbitrary) cartesian products and isomorphic images.
Does Corollary 5 remain valid if we drop the assumption that all groups in the class C are abelian?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A class $\mathcal{V}$ of (Hausdorff) topological groups is called a variety if it is non-empty and closed under taking subgroups, quotient groups, arbitrary Cartesian products (equipped with the Tychonoff product topology and coordinatewise operations), and isomorphic images. For a class $\mathcal{C}$ of topological groups, let $V(\mathcal{C})$ denote the variety generated by $\mathcal{C}$, that is, the intersection of all varieties of topological groups containing $\mathcal{C}$. A topological space is separable if it has a countable dense subset, and metrizable if its topology is induced by some metric.

Suppose $\mathcal{C}$ is a class of separable topological groups (not assumed to be abelian). Must every metrizable topological group in $V(\mathcal{C})$ be separable?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a survey on separability of topological groups. The abelian case is resolved affirmatively (a corollary cited in the survey), but no published resolution of the non-abelian version was located in the search.

status_evidence.title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on separability of topological groups, including the question whether the abelian assumption can be removed in the result that metrizable groups in the variety generated by a class of separable groups are separable.
status_evidence.claim: The non-abelian version is posed as an open problem.
